headline: 'Vendetta': Himachal BJP On FIR Against Kangana Ranaut Over Sonia Gandhi Remark, Congress Responds
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Saturday criticised the Congress government in Himachal Pradesh over the FIR registered against party MP Kangana Ranaut, calling it a political vendetta and alleging the state government was trying to silence critics. Himachal Pradesh Leader of Opposition Jai Ram Thakur said Ranaut’s remarks about Sonia Gandhi and the Gandhi family were her personal views and that everyone has the right to express their opinions in a democracy. Speaking to news agency ANI, Thakur alleged that the Congress government had developed a practice of registering FIRs against people for expressing their views on social media. “Kangana Ranaut has expressed her views through her social media handle. Those may be her personal views, but everyone has the right to express their opinions in a democracy. However, the Congress government in Himachal Pradesh appears to have made it a practice to immediately register FIRs whenever something is posted on social media,” he said. Thakur further alleged that several journalists and individuals had faced similar action and questioned whether the government believed that criminal cases could suppress people’s voices. He also claimed that social media handles operated by the state Congress had published objectionable posts against senior BJP leaders, but no FIRs had been registered despite repeated requests. Meanwhile, BJP spokesperson Sanjay Sharma distanced the party from Ranaut’s social media remarks, saying they reflected her personal opinion and not the BJP’s official position. “Kangana Ranaut is the Member of Parliament from the BJP’s Mandi parliamentary constituency. Whatever she says or writes on her social media platform is her personal opinion and not the party’s official statement,” Sharma told ANI. He added that the FIR was a matter between the complainant and Ranaut and that the court would examine the facts and determine the truth. Congress Defends FIR, Says False Claims To Tarnish Reputation Unacceptable The Congress government in Himachal Pradesh has defended the police action, rejecting the BJP’s allegations of political vendetta. Revenue Minister Jagat Singh Negi said propagating false and baseless claims to tarnish an individual’s reputation was unacceptable. He said Sonia Gandhi’s book was of historical significance as it detailed events spanning several decades. Negi also claimed that the book’s analysis of the roles of the BJP and the RSS had left both organisations rattled. Alleging that the BJP was unable to provide a substantive response to the book’s contents, Negi said the party had resorted to low-level rhetoric. Naresh Chauhan, Principal Media Advisor to the Chief Minister, also criticised Ranaut’s remarks, describing them as unbecoming of her position. He alleged that the actor-turned-politician had a penchant for staying in the headlines and tried to do so by making controversial statements. What Is The FIR Against Kangana Ranaut About? The Shimla Police registered an FIR against Kangana Ranaut on Friday following a complaint by Shimla resident retired Captain Atul Sharma. The case was registered at the Shimla West police station under Sections 196, 353 and 356 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The complaint concerns a series of posts published on November 10 from Ranaut’s verified social media account. The complainant alleged that the posts contained inflammatory insinuations regarding the deaths of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and her sons Sanjay Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi. According to the complaint, one of the posts described Sonia Gandhi as a “mysterious foreign national” who allegedly landed in a cafe abroad before relatives were killed one after another, leaving her as the head of government, followed by the remark: “How convenient”. The complaint also referred to allegations about Maneka Gandhi being abruptly expelled from the family residence following Sanjay Gandhi’s death. The complainant alleged that the posts went beyond political dissent and could promote public hostility, disturb public tranquillity and spread false information. Shimla Superintendent of Police Gaurav Singh had earlier confirmed that the FIR was registered following the complaint and that an investigation would follow.

headline: Panipat man backs out after Canadian woman arrives in India for marriage
content: A 61-year-old Canadian woman who came to Rajasthan to marry a man she befriended on a dating app was left stranded after he allegedly refused to marry her because he found her too old when he met her, police said.The incident took place in Neemrana in Behror district. The police intervened at the request of the Canadian Embassy after the woman approached it.Neemrana SHO Surendra Yadav said that on Friday, police went to BB Builders Society and took the woman and the man to the station for questioning.According to the police, Nitin is a 31-year-old resident of Panipat in Haryana.Nitin, the SHO said, had met the Canadian woman through a dating app and had been in touch with her for around a year. As their relationship grew, they decided to marry.On November 11, the woman arrived in Delhi on a tourist visa.Nitin received her at the airport and brought her to a flat belonging to his maternal uncle and aunt in Neemrana, where she stayed with him for two days.However, when she broached the subject of marriage, Nitin backed out over her age, Yadav said.For now, the woman has been kept at a care centre in Kotputli, and efforts are on to facilitate her return to Canada.Nitin, a teacher at a private school in Panipat, is being questioned.

headline: Pushkar Fair to offer foreign tourists a taste of rural Rajasthan through traditional games
content: Rajasthan's Pushkar attracted more than 1.32 crore domestic tourists and 68,327 foreign visitors in 2025, with the upcoming annual fair set to offer international visitors an opportunity to participate in traditional rural games alongside locals, officials said on Sunday.The Pushkar Fair, scheduled from November 17 to 24, will feature traditional sports, cultural performances and religious events, while a food and handicrafts festival will showcase Rajasthan's culinary and craft heritage.According to Tourism Department data, Pushkar received 76.42 lakh domestic and 59,951 foreign tourists in 2023. The figures increased to 1.24 crore domestic and 74,726 foreign visitors in 2024.In 2026, more than 70.88 lakh domestic tourists and 31,459 foreign visitors had arrived in Pushkar till August, the department said.Tourism Department Joint Director Ajay Sharma said foreign tourists would participate in traditional rural games such as Langdi Tang, Sitoliya and Gilli-Danda during this year's fair.A football match between local participants and foreign tourists is also proposed, besides tug-of-war, kabaddi, volleyball and inter-panchayat samiti rural sports competitions.The fair will also feature camel races, camel and horse dances, turban-tying and moustache competitions, women's pot races and musical chairs.Pushkar Fair nodal officer and Tourism Department Joint Director Dalip Singh Rathore said the Food and Handicrafts Festival would be inaugurated at Shilpgram on November 20 and continue till November 23.The festival will showcase traditional Rajasthani cuisine and handicrafts, providing local artisans and craftsmen a platform to exhibit and sell their products, he said.Religious events, including Maha Aarti and Deepdaan at the ghats of Pushkar lake, will also be organised. Folk artistes from Rajasthan and other states will present traditional music and dance performances.Cultural programmes will begin with the fair's inauguration on November 17, while a mega cultural event, prize distribution for various competitions and the closing ceremony will be held on November 24.Sharma said the fair's identity was rooted in religious faith, folk traditions and rural life, adding that introducing new tourism experiences alongside traditional events would further expand its international appeal.

headline: Pakistan link suspected in Rajasthan railway blast; 2 from Punjab’s Gurdaspur arrested
content: A 21-year-old woman and a man from Punjab's Gurdaspur have been arrested in connection with the November 3 blast on a railway track in Rajasthan's Sri Ganganagar district, with investigators probing suspected links to Pakistan-based handlers, Punjab Police sources said on Sunday.Mahakdeep Kaur and Davinder Singh, both residents of Gurdaspur, were arrested in a joint operation involving the Rajasthan Anti-Terrorism Squad, Sri Ganganagar Police and Punjab Police.Punjab Police sources said the arrests followed a sustained investigation and coordination with Rajasthan agencies. Rajasthan media reports, quoting police officials, said Kaur was allegedly in contact with two Pakistan-based handlers identified by the names 'Chacha' and 'Shah'.Investigators suspect that the handlers used romantic conversations and financial incentives to recruit her. She allegedly received money to carry out the explosion, according to reports.The blast took place around 9.45 pm on November 3 near Ramsinghpur on the Anupgarh-Suratgarh railway line. It damaged the tracks, broke railway sleepers and left a crater at the site. A passenger train had passed through the stretch around 75 minutes before the explosion.Rajasthan Police have alleged possible links to Pakistan's intelligence network, although these connections are still under investigation.Sources said Kaur was living separately from her husband, who is currently lodged in jail in connection with a drug trafficking case. Police suspect that handlers may have targeted women considered vulnerable because of their personal circumstances.According to reports, two weapons, 46 cartridges and Rs 30,000 were recovered from the accused.Three other individuals have also been detained on suspicion of providing logistical support to the operation. They allegedly arranged accommodation, a motorcycle and transport to the blast site.

headline: Union Sports Minister Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya and Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy Unveil Logo and Mascot for 8th Edition of Khelo India Youth Games 2026
content: Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya and Chief Minister of Telangana A. Revanth Reddy today unveiled the logo and mascot for the 8th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG), scheduled to be held in Telangana from December 11 to 22, 2026. Addressing the gathering, Dr. Mandaviya said that Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has placed special emphasis on connecting the youth with sports and integrating sports into the broader vision of the country’s development. CM of Telangana, Shri @revanth_anumula Garu, Ministers in the Telangana government, Shri @Vakiti_srihari Garu, Shri @UttamINC Garu and Union Minister Dr. @mansukhmandviya met Prime Minister @narendramodi. @TelanganaCMO https://t.co/jBCB3PxWQa “The Union Government, under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, is committed to promoting sports. Various competitions, including the Khelo India Youth Games, Beach Games, Winter Games and Tribal Games, are being organised under the Khelo India initiative to encourage greater participation of the younger generation in sports,” Dr. Mandaviya said. The Union Sports Minister and the Telangana Chief Minister also expressed their gratitude to the Prime Minister for his guidance and support in organising the Khelo India Youth Games in Telangana. Dr. Mandaviya further stated that the Union Government, in collaboration with the Telangana Government, would work towards encouraging and inspiring youth to take up sports and contribute to building a strong sporting culture in the country.

headline: Chhattisgarh government introduces high-tech transparency in paddy procurement
content: RAIPUR: The procurement of paddy at Minimum Support Price (MSP) in Chhattisgarh, which began on Sunday, underwent a significant technology-driven overhaul.For the Kharif marketing year 2026–27, the state government has established a comprehensive digital surveillance framework that tracks every stage—from initial farmer registration, weighing, payment, and storage, up to the final supply of milled rice.Utilising tools like biometric authentication, AgriStack farmer IDs, digital crop surveys, electronic weighing scales, and QR codes, the initiative ensures that only genuine farmers sell their produce while minimising any scope for manipulation.To sell paddy this season, registration on the AgriStack portal is compulsory. Farmers must obtain an AgriStack ID (Farmer ID) and link their respective land parcel's (khasra) Farm ID to their unique identity. Procurement eligibility is strictly determined based on the crops recorded and acreage verified through digital crop surveys. Furthermore, AI-based image validation and QR code verification are being deployed to pre-empt fraudulent entries..Paddy politics: Chhattisgarh government’s per-acre aid blunts Congress.Beginning in Kharif 2026–27, 100% scanning of QR codes on rice bags will enable seamless tracking of grain movement from mills to the Food Corporation of India (FCI), the Civil Supplies Corporation, and fair-price shops. This ensures rigorous stock monitoring, bag identification, and strict control over potential diversion.To streamline financial settlements, paddy payments will be transferred directly into farmers' bank accounts via digital channels, with computerised payment receipts generated right at the procurement centres.Additionally, all inbound and outbound logistics data at paddy collection centres will be logged into a web-and-computerised network management system.Purchases will run at Rs 3,100 per quintal (up to 21 quintals per acre) across 3,100 procurement centres, including 360 newly opened centres designed to cut travel time and congestion. headline: Himachal Approves Geriatric Medicine Departments at IGMC Shimla, Tanda and Nerchowk Medical Colleges
content: Specialised healthcare facilities for senior citizens to be strengthened; posts of Assistant Professors and Senior Residents also approved Shimla: In a major initiative to strengthen specialised healthcare services for senior citizens, the Himachal Pradesh government has approved the establishment of dedicated Departments of Geriatric Medicine at three government medical colleges in the state — Indira Gandhi Medical College (IGMC), Shimla, Dr. Rajendra Prasad Government Medical College (RPGMC), Tanda, and Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri Government Medical College (SLBSGMC), Nerchowk. The government has also approved the creation and filling up of requisite posts of Assistant Professors and Senior Residents to ensure the effective functioning of these departments. The initiative aims to address the growing healthcare needs of the elderly population by providing specialised medical facilities for age-related diseases, multiple health complications and other conditions associated with ageing. Geriatric medicine is a specialised branch of healthcare focusing on the diagnosis, treatment and prevention of diseases among older adults. Unlike conventional medical specialities that concentrate on individual organs, it follows a comprehensive approach by considering patients’ overall physical health, mental well-being, functional abilities and social needs. The proposed departments will focus on early diagnosis, appropriate treatment and prevention of age-related illnesses and disabilities. They will also help distinguish between medical conditions and normal ageing-related changes, with the broader objective of improving the quality of life of senior citizens.

headline: BJP Questions Transparency in Mining Lease Allocation, Seeks White Paper
content: Shimla: BJP state spokesperson and MLA D.S. Thakur has questioned the transparency of mining lease allocations under the Congress government in Himachal Pradesh, alleging serious irregularities in the auction process and collection of government revenue. He demanded that the state government issue a comprehensive white paper detailing mining lease allocations, beneficiaries, land allotments and revenue collection across all districts. Raising concerns over a mining lease involving 165 bighas of government land in Chamba district, Thakur said the matter had already been brought up in the Legislative Assembly in March 2025. During the discussion, the Industries Minister had informed the House that the application for the lease dated back to 2015 and a Letter of Intent (LoI) was issued in 2016. The minister had also stated that since 2018, the practice of granting mining leases for more than five bighas of government land without an auction had been discontinued. Questioning the subsequent developments in the case, Thakur sought clarification on how the pending application was dealt with and under which regulatory provisions further approvals were granted. He demanded that the government make all relevant records public. Referring to the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) report, the BJP MLA said Himachal Pradesh had 487 registered mining leases as of March 2023, including 38 for major minerals and 449 for minor minerals. Chamba district accounted for nine of these leases. He demanded that the government disclose the number of new mining leases approved since December 2022, the total government land allocated for mining activities, the number of leases granted through auctions and the revenue generated from each allocation. Thakur also expressed concern over the CAG’s observations regarding revenue collection and regulatory compliance. He pointed out that during the audit period from 2018-19 to 2022-23, the CAG had identified a shortfall of approximately ₹86.38 lakh in contributions to the District Mineral Foundation (DMF) from selected mining leases in Bilaspur, Shimla and Una districts.

headline: Himachal Assembly's Winter Session to Begin in Dharamshala on Monday; BJP Set to Corner Sukhu Government
content: The six-day winter session of the Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly will commence on Monday at Tapovan in Dharamshala, with the proceedings scheduled to begin at 2 pm. The state government will also shift its operations to Dharamshala for the duration of the session, which will continue from November 16 to 21. The winter session is expected to witness intense political confrontations between the ruling Congress and the opposition BJP, with several contentious issues likely to dominate the proceedings. The BJP is preparing to corner the Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu-led government over a range of issues, including the selection process under the Mukhyamantri Apna Parivar Sukhi Parivar scheme, the promised monthly financial assistance of ₹1,500 to women, the implementation of election guarantees and the alleged slow pace of development works across the state. The opposition is also expected to question the government over the status of various welfare schemes, pending development projects and issues affecting the general public. On the other hand, the government is preparing to respond to the opposition’s allegations while highlighting its achievements and progress on various policy initiatives. With both sides gearing up for the final Assembly session of the current legislative term, the proceedings are expected to be politically significant. According to information, legislators have submitted more than 413 questions to the Assembly Secretariat for the session. These questions seek information from the government on the functioning of different departments, implementation of government schemes, progress of development projects, pending works and public grievances.

headline: Himachal Pradesh School Bus Accident: 3 Seriously Injured
content: Three individuals, including the principal of a private school, sustained serious injuries when a school bus veered off course and collided with a road divider on National Highway-5 in Himachal Pradesh's Solan district. The accident occurred late Saturday night while the bus was en route back to Panchkula from Rajgarh, carrying over 50 students, teachers, and staff.Information was available with The Chenab Times that the incident took place near Chakki Mor. The impact of the collision was significant, causing the windows on the driver's side to shatter and narrowly preventing the bus from overturning. In addition to the three individuals with severe injuries, several students reportedly suffered minor injuries.The seriously injured individuals have been identified as Amita, the school principal; Narendra Singla, the chairman; and Meenu, the coordinator. They were transported to a hospital in Panchkula for medical attention via private vehicle. A complaint was lodged with the police by Shilpa Chauhan, a teacher at Litera Heritage School and a resident of Panchkula.According to the teacher's complaint, the driver, identified as Sahil, was operating the vehicle at a high speed and in a negligent manner. The accident occurred around 11 p.m. when the bus struck the road divider. Based on the statement provided by the teacher, the police have registered a case against the driver and initiated further investigation into the matter.The Litera Heritage School, based in Panchkula, had organised an excursion to Rajgarh for its students and staff. The return journey on Saturday night took a critical turn when the accident occurred on the busy National Highway-5, a key route connecting various parts of Himachal Pradesh with neighbouring states. The highway is known for its winding stretches and inclines, requiring careful driving, especially at night.Emergency services were reportedly alerted following the accident, and local authorities and medical personnel arrived at the scene to assist. The injured were promptly attended to, with the most critically wounded being transferred to Panchkula for specialized care. The presence of numerous students on the bus heightened concerns, though fortunately, their injuries were reported as minor.Authorities are expected to conduct a thorough investigation into the accident to determine the precise cause, focusing on aspects such as vehicle maintenance, driver conduct, and road conditions at the time of the incident. The registration of a case against the driver indicates that negligence is a primary line of inquiry for the investigating police team. Such incidents on major highways often prompt reviews of safety protocols and enforcement of traffic regulations by the transport authorities.The area where the accident occurred is a part of Solan district, which lies in the lower hills of Himachal Pradesh. National Highway-5 is a vital artery that facilitates connectivity and transportation for both commuters and commercial vehicles. Accidents on such routes, while unfortunate, often highlight the importance of road safety measures, driver training, and adherence to speed limits, particularly for vehicles carrying passengers, including schoolchildren.The recovery of the injured principal, chairman, and coordinator is being closely monitored. The school administration is likely to provide support to the affected students and staff. The incident serves as a stark reminder of the potential dangers associated with road travel and the critical role of responsible driving in preventing such mishaps. Further details are awaited as the police investigation progresses.

headline: Proposed Himachal-Chandigarh township forces rethink of mining-hit hill restoration plan in Baddi
content: Kullu: The proposed Him-Chandigarh township in Sheetalpur has forced the Himachal Pradesh forest department to redraw its Rs 1.08-crore ecological restoration plan for hills damaged by illegal mining in Baddi, Solan district.The revised plan shifts restoration work away from the mining-affected Sheetalpur region after the land initially identified for rehabilitation was found to overlap with the proposed township.The development follows a communication from the Baddi sub-divisional magistrate to the Himachal Pradesh State Pollution Control Board (HPSPCB) in Feb, informing it that the state cabinet had approved a new township in Sheetalpur.The proposed project overlapped with land identified by the forest department for afforestation, crate-wire retaining structures and check dams. Some of the land had also been transferred to the Himachal Pradesh Housing and Urban Development Authority (HIMUDA), while diversion of additional land was under consideration.The pollution control board subsequently asked the forest department to prepare a revised restoration plan.The financial outlay remains unchanged at Rs 1.08 crore. The plan proposes plantation, soil and moisture conservation measures and bio-engineering interventions to stabilise degraded hill slopes.Plantation and staggered contour trenches are proposed in Dharampur, with additional trenches in plantation areas in Nalagarh. Other measures include dry stone and crate-wire check dams, farm ponds and brushwood check dams along natural drainage channels and gullies.The interventions aim to slow rainwater runoff, arrest soil erosion, trap sediment and improve groundwater recharge. The department has adopted a ridge-to-valley approach, under which treating upper catchments is expected to stabilise mining-damaged slopes downstream.The forest department has cited extensive environmental degradation along the hill slopes connecting Sheetalpur and Dashomajra as the basis for the exercise.The National Green Tribunal proceedings originated from an application filed by Vijay Chandel in 2024, alleging environmental damage caused by illegal excavation in the area.The NGT had earlier directed HPSPCB to submit details of the utilisation of environmental compensation. The board had submitted an action plan in July 2025, prepared in consultation with the forest department.However, implementation was delayed because of complications arising from the proposed township. HPSPCB has now informed the tribunal that it will transfer the entire amount to the forest department to execute the revised plan, subject to the tribunal’s directions.The plantation component includes indigenous species such as khair, siris, shisham, palash and bamboo, whose root systems are expected to help stabilise soil and restore vegetation cover.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: Bulk Drug Park Project Put On Fast Track In Himachal Pradesh
content: Shimla: The work on the Bulk Drug Park coming up at Polian Beet in Haroli, Himachal Pradesh has been put on the fast track, with the Jal Shakti Department granting technical approval of Rs 24.68 crore for the construction of an internal water supply pipeline. The Park is a dream project of Prime Minister Narendra Modi that is coming up in the constituency of Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri. M. Sudha Devi, Principal Secretary of the Industries Department, inspected the site of the Park and held a review meeting with officials from various departments in Una on Saturday to expedite the project. The state government s Jal Shakti Department, Industries Department, Public Works Department, Himachal Pradesh State Electricity Board (HPSEB), Forest Department and the Himachal Pradesh State Industrial Development Corporation are involved in developing the Park. Sudha Devi reviewed the levelling and cutting of 800 acres of land for the first phase of the Park and directed the concerned departments and officials to complete the levelling work by the first month of the next year.Employment for around 20,000 youthThe more than Rs 1900 crore project is expected to provide employment opportunities to around 20,000 youth in Himachal Pradesh. Once completed, the raw materials required for the pharmaceutical sector will be available in India. The Park will also end the country s dependence on China for active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs).Power supply being ensured The Himachal Pradesh Power Transmission Corporation Limited (HPPTCL) is playing a key role in this project. Instructions have been given to prepare a time-bound plan for power supply. So far, 200 acres of the 800-acre land has been levelled in the Beet area. Once the infrastructure is in place, the remaining project work is expected to be completed quickly. The state government has directed the relevant agencies and departments to expedite the work to ensure regular power supply.The HPPTCL has been ordered to issue tenders for surveying the work, laying transmission lines and establishing substations. The tender is expected to be opened on November 28. Sudha Devi has set a target of completing the transmission work by March 2027. The HPSEB has also been directed to expedite work on two other substations to be built in the Park. The Forest Department has been told to complete a tree count to expedite land levelling. The Jal Shakti Department officials say that more than 80% of the work has been completed on the distribution infrastructure for the Park. A tender has also been floated for the internal water distribution network.Will end Chinese dominanceIn 2020, the central government initiated development of three bulk drug parks across the country. One of them is being set up in Haroli in Una district of Himachal Pradesh. Prime Minister Modi laid the foundation stone for the Park on October 13, 2022. The Park is coming up on approximately 1,405 acres, for which the central government has approved a grant of Rs 1,000 crore, with the state government contributing the remaining amount. Approximately 600 acres will be used for the production of APIs. Additionally, 110 plots have been allocated for industrial units producing drug intermediates.Currently, China is the global leader in API production, and this Park is expected to end its dominance. Currently, 70% of India’s APIs come from China. In 2024, APIs worth $2.3 billion were imported from China. The construction of this Park will save foreign exchange and generate employment.The Himachal Pradesh government has formed a high-powered committee and Bulk Drug Park Infrastructure Limited under the Industries Department for this project. The project needs 120 megawatts of power. When the Park’s foundation stone was laid, the state had a BJP government. Subsequently, the Congress government led by Chief Minister Sukhwinder Singh Sukhu has pushed the project forward. Necessary central approvals have been received periodically. The project s biggest hurdle was overcome with the receipt of environmental clearance in September 2025. Now, the work on the project is progressing at a rapid pace. The total investment is estimated to be around Rs 10,000 crore.Also ReadExplainer: What are drug parks and why is India setting them up?400 companies, Rs 8000 cr: Gujarat govt to initiate tender process soon for Jambusar s mega drug park

headline: Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya Palampur wins national award for seed conservation
content: Chaudhary Sarwan Kumar Himachal Pradesh Krishi Vishvavidyalaya, Palampur, has congratulated the Hattee Kisan Sangh of Sirmaur district on winning the prestigious Plant Genome Saviour Community Award, conferred by the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority (PPV&FRA), Government of India. The award recognises the community’s outstanding contribution to conserving seeds.Dr Janardan Singh, Director of Extension Education, CSKHPKV, congratulated the Hattee Kisan Sangh, farmers of Sirmaur and the entire team associated with the achievement. He appreciated their dedicated efforts to conserve indigenous crop varieties and preserve traditional agricultural heritage, saying the national recognition was a matter of pride for Himachal Pradesh. He also acknowledged the contribution of agricultural scientists and Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) personnel in encouraging farmers to participate in biodiversity conservation.The award was presented at a ceremony held in New Delhi on November 12, 2026. The Hattee Kisan Sangh was among only five farming communities selected from across the country for the honour. The award carries a cash prize of Rs 10 lakh, along with a certificate and a memento.The recognition follows the registration of traditional Hattee Dry Ginger (Hattee Saunth), for which the community received a registration certificate in August 2025. Subsequently, an application for the award was submitted in October 2025. A high-level committee from New Delhi also visited Sirmaur to assess the community’s conservation initiatives before finalising the selection.The achievement is the outcome of coordinated efforts involving Dr Pankaj Mittal, Programme Coordinator, Krishi Vigyan Kendra-Sirmaur, and Dr Desh Raj Chaudhary, Dr Ravinder Kumar, Dr Nimit Kumar and Dr Saurabh Sharma from the university headquarters. Their collective efforts and technical support played an important role in securing this prestigious national recognition.Dr Pankaj Mittal said efforts would now be made to secure a Geographical Indication (GI) tag for Hattee Saunth and facilitate the registration of other indigenous seed and plant varieties conserved by farmers in the district. He also highlighted the incentives available to eligible individual farmers under the Plant Genome Saviour Farmer Reward, which carries a cash prize of Rs 1.5 lakh, and the Plant Genome Saviour Farmer Recognition Award, carrying Rs 1 lakh.The national recognition highlights the rich agricultural heritage of the Hattee community and the sustained efforts of local farmers, KVK-Sirmaur and university scientists to conserve traditional crop varieties and protect agricultural biodiversity. It also reinforces the university’s commitment to strengthening farmer-led conservation initiatives and preserving indigenous agricultural resources.

headline: NAGALAND PAVILION INAUGURATED AT THE 45th IITF 2026 IN NEW DELHI
content: NAGALAND PAVILION INAUGURATED AT THE 45th IITF 2026 IN NEW DELHI The Nagaland Pavilion at the India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 was inaugurated by Mercy Epao, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi on 13th November 2026. The Nagaland team is led by Mhonbeni K Nsarangbe, Pavilion Director, Government of Nagaland and altogether 22 entrepreneurs are participating at the 45th edition of the IITF 2026. The inauguration was attended by officials and representatives from various departments, along with participating entrepreneurs, artisans and exhibitors from Nagaland. The dignitaries visited the stalls and interacted with the participants, appreciating their efforts in preserving traditional craftsmanship while creating opportunities for economic growth. The Nagaland Pavilion will highlight the State’s rich heritage, artistic excellence and growing entrepreneurial spirit, offering visitors an opportunity to experience the traditions, creativity and products of Nagaland under one roof. India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO) is organising the trade fair – one of India’s largest trade fairs, bringing together exhibitors and visitors from across the country and abroad. It will run from 13th November 2026 – 27th November 2026, under the theme ‘Vikas aur Virasat.’

headline: JP Nadda reviews development of Rural Health Training Centre in Najafgarh
content: ```html New Delhi: Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri Jagat Prakash Nadda on Friday reviewed the institutional progress and ongoing development of the Rural Health Training Centre (RHTC), Najafgarh, New Delhi, under the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. During the review, the Minister was apprised of the progress made by the institution across hospital and patient care services, diagnostic and support facilities, human resources, academic infrastructure, quality assurance and community-based healthcare delivery. Nadda appreciated the commendable work undertaken by RHTC Najafgarh in strengthening its institutional infrastructure and healthcare services. He observed that the institution was progressing in the right direction and commended the efforts of the RHTC team in taking forward its development initiatives. He also acknowledged the significant contribution of Safdarjung Hospital and the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare in supporting the institution's growth and development. He expressed confidence that the continued efforts and collective commitment of all stakeholders would further strengthen RHTC as an important centre for patient care, medical education and community healthcare, the PIB stated. Strengthening Hospital and Patient Care Services RHTC Najafgarh has recorded substantial patient footfall during the August–October 2026 period. The institution attended to 94,927 patients in its Outpatient Department (OPD) across 10 specialities and provided emergency services to 35,985 patients. The hospital recorded 198 inpatient admissions during this period. The institution also performed 691 surgeries, comprising 101 major and 590 minor surgeries. Its Anti-Rabies Centre and the Snake Bite Treatment facility also provided substantial service during the same time span. The hospital is equipped with labour rooms, a pharmacy with an updated formulary of over 350 medicines, and dedicated Ayurvedic and Dental Clinics, further broadening the range of services available to patients. Expansion of Diagnostic and Support Infrastructure The review further highlighted the strengthening of diagnostic and support services at the institution. The laboratory is NABL-accredited, while the Ultrasound (USG) facility became operational on October 24, 2026, and has conducted 148 scans. The Physiotherapy and Audiometry units are functional, with 252 audiometry tests conducted between August and October 2026. Other important facilities, including the Central Sterile Supply Department (CSSD), Effluent Treatment Plant, Sewage Treatment Plant and Medical Gas Pipeline System, have also been completed. The institution is working towards operationalising the Blood Storage Unit and Mortuary by January 2027. The CT Scan and X-ray facilities are planned to become operational during the first quarter of 2027. Focus on Academic Infrastructure and Quality Assurance RHTC has also strengthened its nursing education and training infrastructure. The ANM Training School has been renovated, with an annual intake capacity of 44 students for its two-year course. The institution also has an ANM hostel with a capacity of 60 beds. The institution has undertaken quality improvement initiatives under the National Quality Assurance Standards (NQAS) for its three Urban Primary Health Centres. Of the 129 identified action points, 105 have been completed, while 24 are in progress. State-level evaluation and certification are targeted for December 2026, followed by national-level evaluation from February 2027 onwards. The institution has also completed several important compliance-related activities, including biomedical waste management certification from the Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC), e-waste management and Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) compliance. Energy, fire, structural and safety audits have been completed, while the water audit is in progress. Future Development Roadmap The review also covered the institution's short-, medium- and long-term development plans. In the short term, RHTC aims to operationalise specialised clinics, including Thalassemia, De-addiction, Adolescent Health, Venereal Disease, Rheumatology and Non-Communicable Disease clinics by December 2026. The medium-term roadmap envisages the establishment of teaching departments in Family Medicine and Emergency Medicine, with a target of operationalisation by the end of the first quarter of 2027. The longer-term vision includes the development of a B.Sc. Nursing College, Allied Health Sciences College, residential hostel and expansion of medical education facilities.
